rationale: Pulp's standalone Development Inspector needs explicit host lifecycle capabilities so stack-owned inspector state is not destroyed while a native event loop can still dispatch callbacks. WindowHost therefore gains conservative append-only virtual queries for deferred close, compositor capture, blocking-loop behavior, and post-stop exit draining. Existing virtual slots remain unchanged, base implementations fail closed, and only Pulp's inspector-aware standalone hosts opt into the new behavior. This is Pulp-specific developer-tool and host integration work with no counterpart framework behavior to backport.
